title: Chapter 8 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of multimedia accessibility, captions, transcripts, and complex images.

questions.question: What is the correct alt text for a purely decorative icon?
questions.explanation: An empty alt attribute hides the image from screen readers.

questions.question: An `` must always have an `alt` attribute, even if empty.
questions.explanation: The `alt` attribute is required; missing it means screen readers may read the file name.

questions.question: Which method is best for providing a long description of a complex chart?
options: Put all data in the `alt` text
Use `aria-describedby` to link to a data table
Add a caption below the image
questions.explanation: `aria-describedby` connects the image to a detailed, structured description.

questions.question: How do you make an inline SVG accessible if it conveys meaningful information?
questions.explanation: `role='img'` and a `<title>` provide the accessible name and role.

questions.question: A search button contains only an SVG magnifying glass. How should it be made accessible?
options: Add `aria-label='Search'` to the button and `aria-hidden='true'` to the SVG
questions.explanation: The button gets the accessible name; the decorative SVG is hidden.

questions.question: The standard file format for captions and subtitles is _____.
questions.explanation: WebVTT (Web Video Text Tracks) is the W3C standard.

questions.question: Which HTML element links a captions file to a video?
questions.explanation: `<track kind="captions">` is the correct element.

questions.question: Captions and subtitles are the same thing.
questions.explanation: Captions include sound effects and speaker identification; subtitles translate dialogue.

questions.question: What does an audio description provide?
options: A text transcript of the audio
Narration of visual details for blind users
questions.explanation: Audio description narrates visual elements that are not obvious from the audio track.

questions.question: Which WCAG level requires captions for prerecorded video?
questions.explanation: WCAG 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) is Level A.

questions.question: Auto‑generated captions from YouTube are fully compliant with WCAG without any editing.
questions.explanation: Auto captions often have inaccuracies and lack speaker identification; they must be reviewed.

questions.question: What is the minimum requirement for audio‑only content (like a podcast) at WCAG A?
questions.explanation: WCAG 1.2.1 requires a transcript for prerecorded audio.

questions.question: When building a custom video player, which ARIA attribute should a play/pause button use to indicate its state?
questions.explanation: `aria-pressed` reflects the toggle state of the button.

questions.question: What should you add to an `<iframe>` embedding a YouTube video to make it more accessible?
questions.explanation: A descriptive `title` helps screen reader users identify the iframe's content.

questions.question: It's acceptable to auto‑play a video with sound when the page loads as long as there's a pause button.
questions.explanation: Auto‑playing audio interferes with screen readers and violates WCAG 1.4.2 (Audio Control).

questions.question: Which of the following is the most universal way to make a bar chart accessible?
options: A data table alongside the chart
questions.explanation: A data table provides precise, navigable, and structured data.

questions.question: How can you provide a text alternative for an infographic?
options: Use a single alt text describing all details
Build the same content in semantic HTML and use the image decoratively
questions.explanation: HTML provides native accessibility; the image can be supplementary.

questions.question: The `<canvas>` element automatically provides an accessible fallback for its content.
questions.explanation: Canvas is inherently inaccessible; developers must provide a custom fallback.

questions.question: What is `aria-describedby` used for with images?
options: To link the image to a longer description element
questions.explanation: It references an element that contains additional descriptive information.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good practice for interactive SVGs (e.g., clickable map)?
options: Make each region focusable and provide accessible names
Avoid keyboard navigation because it's too complex
questions.explanation: Interactive regions must be keyboard accessible with proper roles and labels.
